questions.q: In a corporate restructuring, the total number of employees in Division A and Division B remains strictly constant. Initially, Division A has '$x$' more employees than Division B, and it is given that Division A has exactly $13x$ employees. After a transfer drive, Division B becomes the majority with '$5x$' more employees than Division A. Meanwhile, the average revenue generated per employee in Division B increased from ₹7,12,400 to ₹8,54,880. What is the exact percentage change in the total revenue generated by Division B?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM (Constant Sum Shifting) + Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yeh hai TCS ka asli jaal! Total Revenue = (No. of Employees) $\times$ (Revenue per Employee). Yahan multiply ho raha hai, toh end mein Successive (Theory 2) lagega. Lekin Division B ke employees ka increase directly nahi diya, usko unhone Theory 1 ($A+B=K$) mein chhupa diya hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dono ka percentage shift nikal aur formula me daal de! Employee shift JSM se find kar, baki direct observation.

Mathematically :-
$$ A - B = x \\implies B = 13x - x = 12x \\\\ Gap = x - (-5x) = 6x \\\\ \\Delta Emp = \\frac{6x}{2} = 3x \\\\ \\% \\Delta Emp = \\frac{3x}{12x} = 25\\% \\\\ \\% \\Delta Rev/Emp = \\frac{854880 - 712400}{712400} = 20\\% \\\\ Net = 25 + 20 + \\frac{25 \\times 20}{100} = 50\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute revenue variables generate kar initial stage aur final stage me aur shift detect kar.

Mathematically :-
$$ Rev_1 = 12x \\times 712400 \\\\ Rev_2 = 15x \\times 854880 \\\\ \\frac{Rev_2}{Rev_1} = \\frac{15}{12} \\times \\frac{854880}{712400} = 1.25 \\times 1.2 = 1.5 \\\\ \\Delta = 50\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi do concepts mix hon, unko isolation mein solve kar. Total number ya exact variables ($x$) nikalne ki koshish mat kar, hamesha base fractional values aur percentages pe khel.

List I (Variable Change)List II (Scale Difference)
A. Emp Shift JSM Base1. $25\%$
B. Multiplier Chain Link2. $50\%$ Net

questions.q: The profits of three partners in a business are initially in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. If their respective profits are increased by $50\%$, $40\%$, and $30\%$ respectively, what is the new simplified ratio of their profits?
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, ratios ko sidha multipliers se multiply kar. $2 \times 1.5 = 3$. $3 \times 1.4 = 4.2$. $4 \times 1.3 = 5.2$. Ratio bana $3 : 4.2 : 5.2$. Isko 10 se multiply kar de decimal hatane ke liye: $30 : 42 : 52$. Ab isko 2 se kaat de answer saamne hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ P_1 : P_2 : P_3 = 2 \times 1.5 : 3 \times 1.4 : 4 \times 1.3 \\ = 3 : 4.2 : 5.2 \\ = 30 : 42 : 52 \\ = 15 : 21 : 26 $$

Exam Takeaway: SSC tumhara basics check karta hai ki ratio ko mentally scale karna aata hai ya nahi. 100 maan ke time waste mat karo.

questions.q: In sweet, one-third is sugar. If the price of sugar now is $\frac{7}{6}$ of the previous price, what is the effective percentage increase in the cost of the sweet?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, sweet me $\frac{1}{3}$ hissa sugar hai. Change sirf isi hisse me ho raha hai. Fraction ka direct multiply maar de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Sugar ka price $7/6$ ho gaya matlab increase $1/6$ ka hai. Sweet me sugar ki hissedari $1/3$ hai. Effective net increase $= 1/3 \times 1/6 = 1/18$. Percentage me nikalne ke liye $\times 100$ kar $\implies 100/18 = 50/9 = 100/18\%$ directly options me given hai.

Mathematically :-
$\text{Inc}_s = \frac{7}{6} - 1 = \frac{1}{6}$
$\text{Net Inc} = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{18}$
$\% = \frac{1}{18} \times 100 = \frac{100}{18}\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Maan le total sweet 300g hai. Sugar 100g, non-sugar 200g. Price assume kar. Calculation lamba jayega. Weighted average hi ultimate hai.

Mathematically :-
$\text{Let total} = 300g$
$\text{Sugar} = 100g, \text{Other} = 200g$
$\text{Old Cost} = 100(6) + 200(C)$
$\text{New Cost} = 100(7) + 200(C)$
$\text{Diff} = 100$
$\% = \frac{100}{1800} = \frac{100}{18}\%$

Exam Takeaway: Partial changes nikalne ke liye hamesha (Fraction of weight) $\times$ (Fraction of change) use karo.

ComponentValue
Share$1/3$
Increase$1/6$

questions.q: The present population of a village is 15280. If the number of males increases by 25% and the number of females increases by 15%, then the population will become 18428. The difference between present population of males and females in the village is:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Total increment $18428 - 15280 = 3148$ ka hua hai. Agar pure gaon ki aabadi sirf 15% se badhti, toh increment kam hota. Ye extra gap sirf un aadmio ke 'extra 10%' ki wajah se hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, seedha JSM chipka. Maan le sab 15% hi badhe.
$$15\% \text{ of } 15280 = 2292$$
Asli me increment $3148$ ka hua. Toh extra kitna aaya? $3148 - 2292 = 856$.
Ye 856 extra aadmio ke 10% ki value hai!
$$10\% \text{ of Males} = 856 \implies \text{Males} = 8560$$
Auraten kitni hui? $15280 - 8560 = 6720$.
Difference $= 8560 - 6720 = 1840$. Seconds me question hawa me! Isme 25% bhi leke kar sakte ho aur easy hoga 4 se kaatne me.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Normal books tujhe $x$ aur $y$ equations ($x+y=15280$, $1.25x+1.15y=18428$) sikhayengi. Usme mat fasna, 2 minute lag jayenge.

Exam Takeaway: Base ko hamesha chote percentage par shift kar diya kar jisse deviation nikal ke easily values mil jaaye.

Aman Sir TrickConcept Name
JSM (Deviation)Assume the lower percentage for both variables to find excess easily.

questions.q: If an equal number of social media accounts are created on each day, find the approximate percentage of the accounts whose creation anniversary will fall on 29th February. (Assume accounts created throughout the 20th century and no account deletions).
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: 20th century me $1901$ se $2000$ tak poore $100$ saal hote hain. $2000$ ek leap year hai, toh exactly 25 leap years aayenge. Total din nikal kar 25 ka fraction check karo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Total days denominator me lo aur leap days numerator me. Approximation se $1461$ din me ek 29 Feb aati hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Total Days} = (75 \times 365) + (25 \times 366) = 36525 \\ \text{29th Feb Occurrences} = 25 \\ \% = \frac{25}{36525} \times 100 \\ = \frac{100}{1461} \approx 0.0684 \% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): 400 saal ka general block bhi laga sakte ho but century fixed hai toh exact calculation behtar hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Cycle of 4 years} = (3 \times 365) + 366 = 1461 \text{ days} \\ \text{In 20th century (1901-2000), 2000 is leap.} \\ \text{Total complete 4-year cycles} = 25 \\ \text{Number of 29 Feb} = 25 \times 1 = 25 \\ \text{Percentage} = \frac{25}{25 \times 1461} \times 100 = \frac{100}{1461} \% = 0.0684 \% $$

Exam Takeaway: Calendar based percentage probability me 4 saal ka block (1461 days) hamesha memory me rakho. Shortcut fraction sidha $1/1461$ hota hai if century ends with a leap year.

Time SpanFraction of 29th Feb
4-Year Leap Cycle$\frac{1}{1461}$

questions.q: The cost of a table is 200% more than that of a chair and the cost of a chair is 20% less than that of a cupboard. If the price of each table and chair is decreased by 25%, and the price of a cupboard is increased by 25%, what will be the percentage increase/decrease in the total cost of 4 tables, 5 chairs and 8 shelves?
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Shelf ko 100 man le. Chair 80 hogi. Table $200\%$ zyada yani $80+160=240$. Seedha items me multiply kar aur nayi cost nikal. Calculation sidhi hai koi JSM mat laga kyunki items and rates scattered hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Direct Ratio Mapping.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Shelf (S)} = 100, \quad \text{Chair (C)} = 80, \quad \text{Table (T)} = 240 \\ \text{Old Cost} = 4(240) + 5(80) + 8(100) = 960 + 400 + 800 = 2160 \\ \text{New T} = 240 \times 0.75 = 180 \\ \text{New C} = 80 \times 0.75 = 60 \\ \text{New S} = 100 \times 1.25 = 125 \\ \text{New Cost} = 4(180) + 5(60) + 8(125) = 720 + 300 + 1000 = 2020 \\ \text{Decrease} = 2160 - 2020 = 140 \\ \% = \frac{140}{2160} \times 100 = 6.48\% \approx 6.5\% \downarrow $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Variables ke form me value change.

Mathematically :-
$$ C = 0.8 S, \quad T = C + 2C = 3C = 2.4 S \\ \text{Old Total} = 4(2.4S) + 5(0.8S) + 8S = 9.6S + 4S + 8S = 21.6 S \\ T_{\text{new}} = 0.75(2.4S) = 1.8S \\ C_{\text{new}} = 0.75(0.8S) = 0.6S \\ S_{\text{new}} = 1.25S \\ \text{New Total} = 4(1.8S) + 5(0.6S) + 8(1.25S) = 7.2S + 3S + 10S = 20.2 S \\ \text{Drop} = \frac{21.6S - 20.2S}{21.6S} \times 100 = \frac{1.4}{21.6} \times 100 = 6.48\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Aise questions me base 100 assume karna aur straight line multiply karna hi best rehta hai. Jyada smart banne gaye toh fass jaoge.

questions.q: The prime cost of an article is thrice of raw material. If the cost of raw material is increased in the ratio 5:12 and cost of manufacturing expenses is increased in the ratio 4:5. If the initial cost is 6 then find the final cost?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, total Prime Cost do chizon se banti hai: Raw Material aur Manufacturing. Hamein relation break karna aana chahiye bina equations likhe. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Initial prime cost 6 di hai, jo Raw (RM) ka 3 guna hai. Yani RM = 2 hoga. Toh bachi hui cost Manufacturing (Mfg) hogi = 4 (Kyunki $2+4=6$). Ab scale laga! RM 5:12 me badha, yani agar RM pehle 5 tha toh 12 hua. Yahan hamara RM 2 hai, toh kitna hoga? $\frac{12}{5} \times 2 = 4.8$. Mfg 4:5 me badha. Hamara Mfg 4 hi hai, toh badh kar seedha 5 ho jayega. Nayi Final Cost = Naya RM + Naya Mfg = $4.8 + 5 = 9.8$. Seedha aur sateek! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Cost equations variables me maan le $3x, x, 2x$ aur fir fractions me ghoomta reh. Answer phir bhi $9.8$ hi aayega. Exam Takeaway: Ratio shifting ko directly split values par laga diya kar.
ComponentInitialFinal (Scaled)
Raw Material24.8
Manufacturing45

questions.q: In an examination a candidate had to sit for three papers A, B, and C. The candidate secured $70\%$ marks in Paper A, $80\%$ marks in Paper B, and $50\%$ marks in Paper C. If the weightage assigned to Papers A, B, and C were $30\%$, $60\%$ and $20\%$, respectively, then find the weighted percentage of marks obtained by the candidate, when all the three papers were taken together?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, options $70\%$ ke aaspas ghoom rahe hain. Weightage ratio $3:6:2$ hai. Paper B ($80\%$) ka wazan sabse jyada hai, toh average pakka $70$ se upar khiskega aur $80$ ki taraf inclined hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Weightage ka ratio bana le $3:6:2$. Base average $70\%$ maan le. A pe deviation $0$, B par deviation $+10\%$ hai ($6$ weight pe = $+60$), C par deviation $-20\%$ hai ($2$ weight pe = $-40$). Net deviation $+20$ aaya. Isko total weight $11$ me baant de. Khatam!

Mathematically :-
$$ Base = 70\\% \\\\ Dev_A = 3 \\times 0 = 0 \\\\ Dev_B = 6 \\times (+10) = +60 \\\\ Dev_C = 2 \\times (-20) = -40 \\\\ Net \\ Dev = +20 \\\\ Avg = 70 + \\frac{20}{11} = 71.81\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic weighted average laga. Pura divide mat kar, $11 \times 71$ hota hai $781$, uske thoda aage $71.81$ dikh raha hai.

Mathematically :-
$$ \\frac{3 \\times 70 + 6 \\times 80 + 2 \\times 50}{3+6+2} \\\\ = \\frac{210 + 480 + 100}{11} \\\\ = \\frac{790}{11} = 71.81\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha percentages ya weights ko chote ratio me kaat liya kar, calculation aadhi ho jayegi aur time bachega!

List I (Variable)List II (Value)
A. Base Average1. $70\%$
B. Net Deviation Shift2. $+\frac{20}{11}$

questions.q: The salary of a person is ₹30,000. It increases first by $2k\%$ and then again by $k\%$, making his new salary ₹44,850. If his original salary was instead decreased by $2k\%$ and then further decreased by $k\%$, what would his new salary be?
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, Final / Initial = $\frac{44850}{30000} = 1.495$. Matlab lagbhag $50\%$ ka growth hua hai successive me. Equation mat bana, Hit and trial best hai. $k=15$ lo, toh $+30\%$ aur $+15\%$ ka net lagbhag $49.5\%$ fit baith gaya!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Net Increase} = \frac{44850 - 30000}{30000} = 49.5\% \\ 2k + k + \frac{2k^2}{100} = 49.5 \implies k = 15 \text{ (by Observation)} \\ \text{Decrease } 1 = 30000 \times (1 - 0.30) = 21000 \\ \text{Decrease } 2 = 21000 \times (1 - 0.15) = 17850 $$

Exam Takeaway: Successive increase/decrease me agar exact formula lagane bethe toh quadratic banegi. Smart assumption + Hit & Trial rules the exam!

questions.q: Kartik saves $20 \%$ of his monthly income while he spends the remaining amount on food, rent, education, and shopping. He spends $15 \%$ of his income on food, while Rs. 12,800 is spent on rent, Rs. 32,000 on education, and Rs. 7,200 on shopping. The amount spent on shopping is $11.25 \%$ of the total expenditure. How much money (in Rs.) is spent on food?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dhyan de bhai, Shopping total expenditure ka $11.25 \%$ diya hai. Aur $11.25 \%$ fraction me $9/80$ hota hai. Waha se directly total expenditure aayega jisko reverse use karke Food ki value mil jayegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Given percentage se independent unit nikalo, baki extra values faltu hain unko ignore karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Shopping} = 11.25 \% \text{ of Total Expenditure} \\ 7200 = \frac{9}{80} \times \text{Total Exp.} \\ \text{Total Exp.} = \frac{7200 \times 80}{9} = 64000 \\ \text{Savings} = 20 \%, \text{ so Exp.} = 80 \% \text{ of Income} \\ 80 \% \text{ of Income} = 64000 \implies 100 \% \text{ Income} = 80000 \\ \text{Food Spend} = 15 \% \text{ of } 80000 = 12000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fractional setup banakar variables dhundo par concept wahi rahega.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Income} = I \\ \text{Expenditure} = 0.8 I \\ \text{Shopping} = 0.1125 \times (0.8 I) = 7200 \\ \frac{1125}{10000} \times 0.8 I = 7200 \\ \frac{9}{80} \times \frac{4}{5} I = 7200 \\ \frac{36}{400} I = 7200 \implies I = \frac{7200 \times 400}{36} = 80000 \\ \text{Food} = 0.15 \times 80000 = 12000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Data trick me mat fasna! Rent aur Education ki given values totally irrelevant thi aur sirf time waste karne ke liye di gayi thi.

Link ConnectionMathematical Jump
Shopping $\rightarrow$ Exp$7200 \times (80/9) = 64000$
Exp $\rightarrow$ Income$64000 \times (5/4) = 80000$

questions.q: The price of fuel decreases by 55%, 55%, and 55% in three successive months, but increases by 65% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease (rounded off to two decimal places) in the price of fuel in the fourth month, as compared to its original price?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Lagatar 3 baar 55% girne se value zameen par aa jayegi. Uspe chotu sa 65% ka increment ghanta fark nahi daalega. Answer bhayankar decrease (around 85%) hi aayega. Isme ratio method calc hoga bahut zyada and ganda wala so approx leke chalo. so always prefer this method for large changes

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, formula wagaira sab bhool ja, seedha decimals multiplier laga. 55% gira yani $0.45$ bacha.
Net multiplier = $0.45 \times 0.45 \times 0.45 \times 1.65$.
$$0.091125 \times 1.65 \approx 0.1503$$
Yani original value ka lagbhag $15.04\%$ hi bacha hai. Toh decrease kitna hua? $100 - 15.04 = 84.96\%$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Yahan $X + Y + \frac{XY}{100}$ wala formula lagana apne pairo par kulhadi maarne jaisa hai. Chain reaction decimals me chalana hi padega.

Exam Takeaway: TCS ke successive traps me decimals ko lagbhag 2 places tak approximate karke seedha multiply kar.

TopicShortcut
Successive ChangeUse multiplier $(1 \pm \frac{r}{100})$ instead of formulas.

questions.q: A fruit seller had total (X+50) mangoes and apples. He sold 20% mangoes to A, 40% of remaining to B and had 48 mangoes left. Similarly, he sold 40% apples to A, 100 apples to B and had 10% apples left. Find (X+500).
questions.s:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, dono fruits ka track ek dum alag hai, mangoes me seedha percentage successive hai aur apples me percentage ke beech absolute number (100) mixed hai. Dono ko alag alag handle kar!

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Mangoes(M): 20\% bika (bacha 80\%), fir 40\% bika (bacha 60\%). Equate kar de: $M \times 0.8 \times 0.6 = 48 \implies 0.48M = 48 \implies M = 100$.
Apples(A): 40\% becha toh bacha 60\%. Ab isme se 100 beche toh end me 10\% bache. Equation bani $0.6A - 100 = 0.1A \implies 0.5A = 100 \implies A = 200$. Total fruits (X+50) hue $100+200 = 300$. Yaha se X = 250 aaya. Pucha X+500 hai, yani $250+500 = 750$.

**Successive Change (The Chain Reaction) & Unitary Scaling.

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Mangoes aur Apples dono ke events bilkul independent hain. Exam me variable `X` dekh kar ghabrana nahi hai. Sabse best hack hai ki pehle individual fruits ki total sankhya percentage ya ratio se nikal lo, aur last me unko add karke `X+50` se equate kar do. Tune jo 3 methods diye hain, aao sabka post-mortem karte hain.

Method 1 (Percentage Base Shift - Ninja Technique):
Mangoes: Let total = 100\%.
Remaining after 20\% sold = 80\%.
Remaining after 40\% of 80\% sold = 80\% \times 60\% = 48\%.
ATQ, 48\% \equiv 48 \Rightarrow 100\% \equiv 100 mangoes.

Apples: Let total = 100\%.
Sold to A = 40\%. Bacha hua 60\%.
Ab isme se 100 apples B ko diye, toh 10\% bache.
Iska sidha observation hai: 60\% - 10\% = 50\%. Ye 50\% hi 100 apples ke barabar hain!
50\% \equiv 100 \Rightarrow 100\% \equiv 200 apples.

Total fruits = 100 + 200 = 300.
So, X + 50 = 300 \Rightarrow X = 250.
Find: X + 500 = 250 + 500 = 750.

Method 2 (Fractional Successive Ratio - Exam Approach):
Mangoes (Successive Change):
20\% = \frac{1}{5} (Base shift: 5 se 4), 40\% = \frac{2}{5} (Base shift: 5 se 3).
InitialFinal
54
53
2512
12 units \equiv 48 \Rightarrow 1 unit = 4.
Total Mangoes = 25 \times 4 = 100.

Apples (Direct Observation):
Total = 100\%. Sold to A = 40\%, Remaining = 10\%.
Consumed percentage without absolute value = 40\% + 10\% = 50\%.
Rest 50\% is exactly the 100 apples given to B.
50\% \equiv 100 \Rightarrow 100\% = 200.
Total = 300, X = 250, Ans = 750.

Method 3 (Basic Variable Equation - The Trap):
Ye teri 3rd image wala approach hai, jo ekdum basic hai. Exam me ye nahi lagana hai!
Mangoes = 100 (derived). Total fruits = X + 50.
So, Total Apples = (X + 50) - 100 = (X - 50).
ATQ for apples:
Sold 40\% (i.e. \frac{2}{5}), remaining = \frac{3}{5}.
(X - 50) \times \frac{3}{5} - 100 = (X - 50) \times \frac{1}{10}
(X - 50) \times \frac{3}{5} - (X - 50) \times \frac{1}{10} = 100
(X - 50) \times \frac{1}{2} = 100
(X - 50) = 200 \Rightarrow X = 250.
Bhai, isme expression balance karne me time jayega. It's a pure waste of 30-40 seconds.


Future Exam Takeaway (Hack Observation):
Exam me hamesha Method 1 ya 2 lagana hai. Jab question me do alag-alag items (Mangoes aur Apples) ho, toh starting ke combined variable (X+50) ko temporarily bhool jao. Individual parts ko 100\% base ya ratio base par solve karo, unki real values nikal kar last me combine karo. Variables ke jaal me tab tak nahi fasna jab tak strictly necessary na ho!

questions.q: In a village, there are two candidates in an election. $20\%$ of the registered voters did not vote, and 1,792 votes were declared invalid. The winning candidate secured $42\%$ of the TOTAL registered votes and won by 3,584 votes. In the neighboring city of Lucknow, the total registered voters are 3 times that of the village. During an election in Lucknow, 4,400 votes were declared invalid, and the winner secured $58\%$ of the valid votes. What is the difference between the valid votes secured by the winning and losing candidates in Lucknow?
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, lamba question dekh ke darna nahi hai, parts me tod. Village mein Winner ko total ka $42\%$ mila. Loser ko kya mila hoga? Total polled me se invalid aur winner hata de. Baad me Lucknow ka factor nikal lenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Village Voters} = T \\ \text{Winner (W)} = 42\% T \\ \text{Loser (L)} = (80\% T - 1792) - 42\% T = 38\% T - 1792 \\ W - L = 4\% T + 1792 = 3584 \\ 4\% T = 1792 \implies T = 44800 \\ \text{Lucknow Voters} = 44800 \times 3 = 134400 \\ \text{Lucknow Valid} = 134400 - 4400 = 130000 \\ \text{Lucknow Margin} = (58\% - 42\%) \times 130000 = 16\% \times 130000 = 20800 $$

Exam Takeaway: Bade statements bas exam hall me pressure banane ke liye hote hain, concepts aur direct equations pakde rakh!

questions.q: P's income is 150 percent of Q's income and P's expenditure is 60 percent of Q's expenditure. If Q saves 20 percent of his income, then how much percentage does P save of his own income?
questions.s:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 5. Unitary Scaling

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, P aur Q ki income ka ratio 3:2 hai. Options integers me hain, toh calculation easy karne ke liye base ko 300 aur 200 maan le taaki zeroes kat jayein aur decimal ka lafda na rahe.

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Q ki income 200 maan. Usne 20\% bachaya, yani 40 bachaya, toh kharcha hua 160. P ka kharcha Q ke kharche (160) ka 60\% hai, matlab $160 \times 0.6 = 96$. P ki income 300 thi, usme se 96 udaya toh bacha 204. Seedha percentage nikal: $\frac{204}{300} \times 100 = 68\%$.

**Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Agar tu x aur y variables banayega, toh linear equations fasa dengi. Ratio base-shifting laga. $Income - Expenditure = Savings$ ka base fraction hi set kar le. Bina x-y ke values assume karna hi real CGL preparation hai.

**Exam Takeaway:** Base values aisi assume kar jisme zeroes jyada hon. Percentage calculations me decimals se bachna hi speed badhata hai.

Calculation StepValue
A. Q's Expenditure1. $200 - 40 = 160$
B. P's Expenditure2. $160 \times 0.60 = 96$
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling (Ratio Base Shifting)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, P aur Q ki income ka ratio 3:2 hai. Yahan hume do alag ratios (Income aur Expenditure) ko ek same scale par laana hai bina variables (x, y) maane. Is ninja technique ko 'Make it Equal and Scale' kehte hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Humare paas do alag ratios hain:
Income (I) $\rightarrow$ P : Q = 3 : 2
Expenditure (E) $\rightarrow$ P : Q = 3 : 5

Condition: Q saves 20% of his income. Yani Q ka kharcha (E) uski income ka 80% hai. Toh Q ke liye: I : E = 100 : 80 = 5 : 4.
Bas ab hume Q ki values ko 5 : 4 ke ratio me set karna hai.

Step 1: Q ko pehle barabar (Equal) kar le.
Income ko 5 se aur Expenditure ko 2 se multiply kar:
I $\rightarrow$ 15 : 10
E $\rightarrow$ 6 : 10

Step 2: Ab Q ko 5 : 4 ke scale par set kar de.
I ko 5 se, E ko 4 se multiply kar:
I $\rightarrow$ (15 $\times$ 5) : (10 $\times$ 5) $\rightarrow$ 75 : 50
E $\rightarrow$ (6 $\times$ 4) : (10 $\times$ 4) $\rightarrow$ 24 : 40

Step 3: Magic Happens!
Check kar, Q ki income 50 hai aur kharcha 40 (jo ki 80% hai). Condition set!
Ab P ka data utha:
P Income = 75, P Expenditure = 24 $\rightarrow$ Savings = 75 - 24 = 51.
Percentage Saving = $\frac{51}{75} \times 100 = \frac{17}{25} \times 100 = 17 \times 4 = 68\%$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Q ki 5 units (E) = 80% of Q's Income (2 units of I).
So, $5E = \frac{4}{5} \times 2I \implies 5E = \frac{8}{5} I \implies 1E = \frac{8}{25} I$.
P ka Kharcha = $3E = 3 \times \frac{8}{25} I = \frac{24}{25} I$.
P ki Income = $3I$. P ki Bachat = $3I - \frac{24}{25}I = \frac{51}{25}I$.
Savings % = $\frac{\frac{51}{25}I}{3I} \times 100 = \frac{17}{25} \times 100 = 68\%$.

Exam Takeaway: Method 1 is ultimate! Jab bhi do ratios ko aapas me fraction se link karna ho, toh LCM le kar Equal kar le, phir required ratio se Scale kar de. Zero variable, full marks!

questions.q: Sum of A and B is $100\%$ more than the sum of C and D. C is $20\%$ more than D. If A is $200\%$ more than B and D=500, then what is the value of A? (CHSL TIER I - 24/11/2025 - SHIFT 3)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, A, B se $200\%$ jyada hai yani A aur B ka ratio $3:1$ baithta hai. Iska matlab A ki value hamesha $3$ ka multiple hogi. Options me $1650$ aur $1200$ hi available hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Step by step ulta chal. Data ko link karte jao bas! Mathematically :- $$ D = 500 \\ C = 500 \times 1.2 = 600 \\ C + D = 1100 \\ A + B = 2 \times 1100 = 2200 \\ A:B = 3:1 \implies 4 \text{ units} = 2200 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 550 \\ A = 3 \times 550 = 1650 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variables equations banana padega. Mathematically :- $$ C = 1.2D = 600 \\ A + B = 2(C + D) = 2200 \\ A = B + 2B = 3B \\ 3B + B = 2200 \implies 4B = 2200 \implies B = 550 \\ A = 3B = 1650 $$

Exam Takeaway: Statements ko end se solve karna jab variables cascading chain me de rakhe hon, fast aur error-free hota hai.

Variable MappingDerived Value
A. Base D $\rightarrow$ C1. $500 \implies 600$
B. $(C+D)$ $\rightarrow$ $(A+B)$2. $1100 \implies 2200$

questions.q: A reduction of $7.5\%$ in the cost price of a commodity enables a shopkeeper to purchase 15 kg more than what he previously purchased for a sum of $\text{Rs. } 7,400$. In order to make a profit of $32.5\%$ on the pre-reduction cost price of the commodity, at what price (in Rs) per kg should the commodity be sold?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 1. CPR (Constant Product Ratio)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ye SSC ka all-time favorite format hai. Jab kharcha fixed (Rs 7400) rakha ho, toh price me aayi girawat ka sidha faida hume bachay gye paison me hota hai. Wahin se naya price nikalta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Buyer ne paise bacha liye hote agar wo utna hi quantity leta. Us shift se current rate nikal lo aur original pe pahoncho.

Mathematically :-
$$ Saved = 7400 \\times 7.5\\% = 555 \\\\ P_{new} = \\frac{555}{15} = 37 \\\\ P_{old} \\times 92.5\\% = 37 \\implies P_{old} = 40 \\\\ SP_{req} = 40 \\times (1 + 32.5\\%) = 40 \\times \\frac{53}{40} = 53 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic variables banao. Ratio solve karo lamba root method aayega.

Mathematically :-
$$ \\frac{7400}{P_{new}} - \\frac{7400}{P_{old}} = 15 \\\\ P_{new} = P_{old} \\times 0.925 \\\\ \\frac{7400}{0.925 P_{old}} - \\frac{7400}{P_{old}} = 15 \\\\ P_{old} = 40 \\implies SP = 53 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi Quantity increase pucha ho, seedha "Total Amount ka $\%$ girawat / Extra Quantity" = "Current Reduced Price" nikal kar base shift karo.

List I (Price Phase)List II (Value per kg)
A. Reduced Cost Price1. $\text{Rs. } 37$
B. Original Cost Price2. $\text{Rs. } 40$

questions.q: A metallurgist mixes two alloys, A and B, to make a total of 80 kg of a new mixture. Alloy A contains 15% copper, and Alloy B contains 25% copper. If the final mixture contains a total of 15 kg of copper, what is the difference in the weights of Alloy A and Alloy B used?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, mixture dekh ke Alligation yaad aata hai, lekin JSM yahan zyada tez hai kyunki total quantity pata hai. Minimum 15% copper toh dono me hai na!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Base copper 15% maan le. 80kg ka 15% = 12kg. Lekin question bola total 15kg copper hai. Extra kitna? 3kg. Ye extra aya kahan se? Alloy B ke extra 10% (25-15) se. Toh B ka 10% = 3kg $\implies$ B = 30kg. A bacha 50kg. Difference 20kg.

Mathematically :-
$\text{Base} = 15\%$
$\text{Assumed} = 80 \times 0.15 = 12$
$\text{Actual} = 15$
$\text{Extra} = 3$
$10\% \text{ of } B = 3 \implies B = 30$
$A = 50$
$\text{Diff} = 20$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Alligation se karega toh pehle final mixture ka overall percentage nikal, fraction aayega, usme alligate karega toh time lag jayega.

Mathematically :-
$\text{Total Cu } \% = \frac{15}{80} \times 100 = 18.75\%$
$\text{Ratio A:B} = (25 - 18.75) : (18.75 - 15) = 6.25 : 3.75 = 5:3$
$A = 50, B = 30$
$A - B = 20$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi do alag percentages ho aur unka overall total number me diya ho, hamesha JSM thok dena, alligation se fast hai.

AlloyJSM Split
B (25%)$15\% + 10\%$

questions.q:
A massive commercial cargo ship has a strictly fixed maximum payload capacity dedicated entirely to carrying only two types of containers: Type-A (Chemicals) and Type-B (Textiles). The total payload weight of a container type is determined by multiplying the "Weight per container" by the "Number of containers". Initially, the total payload weight of Type-A was exactly 33.33% of the total payload weight of Type-B.

Due to new safety regulations, the weight of "each" Type-A container is increased by 15%, while the company strictly keeps the number of Type-A containers unchanged. To keep the ship's total payload weight exactly at its fixed maximum capacity, by what percentage must the overall payload weight of Type-B containers be reduced?
questions.s: Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Layer 1: Constant Base Expansion: Weight/Box $\times$ No. of Boxes = Total Weight ($A \times B = K$). Layer 2: JSM / The Zero-Sum Game: Total Weight A + Total Weight B = Fixed Ship Capacity ($A + B = K$). The "Pen-Free" Observation First: Dekh bhai, dimaag ko bilkul shant rakh. SSC wale language badal ke darayenge, par core engine wahi hai. Type-A containers $33.33\%$ hain Type-B ke. Yani Ratio $1:3$ hai. Type-A ke har ek dabbe ka wazan $15\%$ badha aur dabbon ki sankhya same rahi (Layer 1). Iska seedha sa matlab hai ki Type-A ka Total Wazan exact $15\%$ se badh gaya! Ab total jahaz ka wazan fix rakhna hai, toh Type-A ne jitna wazan badhaya, Type-B ko exactly utna hi wazan kam karna padega (Layer 2). 10 second ka game hai! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Ratio Balancer): Ratio of Total Weights $\rightarrow$ Type-A : Type-B = $1 : 3$. Type-A ka naya gain = $1$ unit ka $15\%$ = $+0.15$ units. Kyuki Jahaz ka total wazan (Capacity) fix hai, jo wazan Type-A ne gain kiya, wo Type-B ko lose karna padega. Type-B ka reduction = $-0.15$ units. Percentage Reduction in Type-B = $\frac{\text{Actual Reduction}}{\text{Type-B Base}} \times 100$ $\Rightarrow \frac{0.15}{3} \times 100 =$ $5\%$. Option 2 is strictly correct. Method 2 (Concept Builder - Assumption Method): Let Total Weight of Type-B = $300$ tons. Since Type-A is $33.33\%$ (or $1/3$) of B, Type-A = $100$ tons. Total Ship Capacity = $100 + 300 = 400$ tons. Type-A ka wazan $15\%$ badh gaya $\Rightarrow$ Naya Type-A = $115$ tons. Ship capacity $400$ fix rakhni hai, toh Naya Type-B = $400 - 115 = 285$ tons. Type-B mein kitni girawat aayi? $300 \rightarrow 285$, yani $15$ tons ki girawat aayi $300$ par. Percentage = $\frac{15}{300} \times 100 =$ $5\%$. Future Exam Takeaway: Language chahe "Cargo Capacity" ki ho ya "Server/Data Bandwidth" ki, agar ek component $A \times B$ se bana hai aur unka overall sum fixed hai, toh direct base ratio likho aur shift ko transfer kar do. Ye Double-Engine hacks hi top rankers ka secret weapon hain!

questions.q: In a co-educational school there are 15 more girls than boys. If the number of girls is increased by $10\%$ and the number of boys is also increased by $16\%$, there would be 9 more girls than boys. What is the number of students in the school ?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.
Pen-Free Observation : Dekh bhai, difference 15 se 9 ho gaya matlab 6 ka gap boys ne apne extra 6% growth se cover kiya. Sath mein unhone 15 extra girls ka 10% (1.5) bhi nullify kiya hoga. So 6% of Boys is directly 7.5!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Mental Deviation. Mathematically :-

$$ \Delta \text{Diff} = 15 - 9 = 6 \\ 16\% B - 10\% G = 6 \\ 16\% B - 10\% (B + 15) = 6 \\ 6\% B - 1.5 = 6 \\ 6\% B = 7.5 \implies B = 125 \\ \text{Total} = 125 + (125 + 15) = 265 $$


Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, 2 linear equations ban rahi hain, G ko $(B + 15)$ rakh aur substitution maar ke khatam kar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Variable elimination. Mathematically :-
$$1.1(B + 15) - 1.16B = 9$$
$$16.5 - 0.06B = 9$$
$$0.06B = 7.5 \Rightarrow B = 125$$
$$Total = 125 + (125+15) = 265$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Base assumptions from options. Mathematically :-
$$Total = 265$$
$$G + B = 265 \text{ and } G - B = 15$$
$$G = 140, B = 125$$
$$140 \times 1.1 - 125 \times 1.16 = 154 - 145 = 9$$

Exam Takeaway: Option split karke mentally verify karna linear equations se bhi fast hota hai kai baar.

List IList II
Option validationCheck pairs that sum to option and difference is 15.

questions.q: 2/5th of the voters promise to vote for A and the rest promised to vote for B. Of these, on the last day $15\%$ of the voters went back of their promise to vote for A and $25\%$ of voters went back of their promise to vote for B, and A lost by 200 votes. Then, the total number of voters is?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Decimal na aaye isliye ek heavy base $1000x$ lele aur swap ki matrix chala de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): A ko 400x, B ko 600x promise the. A ke $15\%$ ($60x$) B ko mile. B ke $25\%$ ($150x$) A ko mile. Final A $= 400 - 60 + 150 = 490x$. Final B $= 600 - 150 + 60 = 510x$. Haar/Jeet diff $= 20x$. Diya hai $20x = 200 \Rightarrow x=10$. Total votes $= 1000x = 10000$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Shift matrix directly likh: $+150-60 = +90$ net shift A ke favour me. Naya A $= 400+90 = 490$. Diff nikal lo.

Exam Takeaway: Values assume karte time zeros ka bharpoor istemal karo taaki fractions aur decimals ke jaal me na faso.

CandidateFinal Tally
A$490x$
B$510x$

questions.q: A, B and C spend $75\%$, $80\%$ and $90\%$ of their incomes, respectively. If their savings are in the ratio 4: 6: 5 and the difference between the incomes of A and C is 25,500, then the income of B is?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, expenditure percentage diya hai par ratio savings ka diya hai. Ulta sochna padega. Incomes nikalne ke liye savings ko uske percentage se bhag (divide) de. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Pehle saving percentage nikal: A=$25\%$, B=$20\%$, C=$10\%$. Ab direct Income ratio likh = $\frac{\text{Saving Ratio}}{\text{Saving } \%}$. Yani $\frac{4}{25} : \frac{6}{20} : \frac{5}{10}$. Percentage hata de kyunki ratio me common cut jayega. Bacha $\frac{4}{25} : \frac{6}{20} : \frac{5}{10} \implies \frac{16}{100} : \frac{30}{100} : \frac{50}{100}$. Base 100 cut gaya, naya ratio $16:30:50$ yaani $8:15:25$ aagaya. A aur C ka difference $25 - 8 = 17$ unit hai. Sawal kehta hai ye $25500$ hai. $1$ unit = $1500$. B ki income puchi hai ($15$ unit), toh $15 \times 1500 = 22500$ answer hoga! Bawal cheez hai ye ratio base shifting. Method 2 (Concept Builder): A ki income ka $25\% = 4x \implies A = 16x$. B ki income ka $20\% = 6x \implies B = 30x$. C ki income ka $10\% = 5x \implies C = 50x$. Income ratio $16x : 30x : 50x = 8 : 15 : 25$. Diff $25 - 8 = 17$ unit $= 25500$. $1$ unit $= 1500$. $B = 15 \times 1500 = 22500$. Exam Takeaway: Expenditure diya ho aur saving ratio pooche to turant $100 - x$ karke equate kar liya kar.
PersonIncome Ratio
A$4 / 25\% = 16$
B$6 / 20\% = 30$
C$5 / 10\% = 50$

questions.q: Rishabh spends three fourth of his income. His income increases by $2x\%$ and his expenditure also increases by $x\%$. If the percentage of increase in his savings is $50\%$, then find value of $3.75x\%$ of 1440.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ye JSM ka sabse bawal application hai. Income ke components Expenditure aur Savings hote hain, toh unko as a weighted ratio treat karke sidhi deviation ki equation lagao. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $\frac{3}{4}$ spend karne ka matlab Income 4, Exp 3, aur Saving 1. Equation likh: $\text{Income change} = \text{Exp change} + \text{Saving change}$. Base variables lagao: $4 \times (2x) = 3 \times (x) + 1 \times (50)$. Solve kar: $8x = 3x + 50 \implies 5x = 50 \implies x = 10$. Hame calculate karna hai $3.75x\%$ of 1440. Jab x 10 hai, toh ye $37.5\%$ ban jayega. $37.5\%$ ko hum pyaar se $\frac{3}{8}$ bulate hain. $\frac{3}{8} \times 1440 = 3 \times 180 = 540$. Examiner confuse karna chahta hai, tu uda de! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Income = 400. Exp = 300. Saving = 100. New Saving = 150 (50% badhi). New Exp = $300 + 3x$. New Income = $400 + 8x$. Relation: New Income = New Exp + New Saving. $400 + 8x = 300 + 3x + 150$. $5x = 50 \implies x = 10$. Wahi result aaya, bas thoda zyada likhna pada. Exam Takeaway: Ratio ko sidha percentages ke base weights par equation bana diya kar, bada fast x ki value aayegi.
CalculationOutput
1. Found 'x'10
2. Final Percent$37.5\% = \frac{3}{8}$

questions.q: The population of a village 4 years ago was 3,20,000. Due to migration to cities, it decreases at the rate of 5% every year. Find the decrease in its population in the last 4 years.
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, $5\%$ decrease ko 4 baar multiply karna mout hai. Digital Sum (DS) laga! 320000 ka DS 5 hai. Multiplier $0.95$ ka DS 5 hai. Toh New Pop ka DS = $5 \times 5^4 = 5^5$. $5^2 = 25 \implies 7$. $5^5 = 25 \times 25 \times 5 \implies 7 \times 7 \times 5 = 49 \times 5 \implies 4 \times 5 = 20 \implies 2$. Drop = $5 - 2 = 3$. Options me DS 3 sirf ek ka hai: 59358.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Digital Sum completely replaces calculation.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Old Pop DS} = 3+2+0 = 5 \\ \text{Factor DS} = 1 - 0.05 = 0.95 \implies 14 \implies 5 \\ \text{New Pop DS} = 5 \times (5)^4 = 5 \times 625 \implies 5 \times 13 \implies 5 \times 4 = 20 \implies 2 \\ \text{Decrease DS} = 5 - 2 = 3 \\ \text{Check Opt 2:} 5+9+3+5+8 = 30 \implies 3 \text{ (Match!)} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Fractional multipliers approach.

Mathematically :-
$$ A = P \left(1 - \frac{r}{100}\right)^t \\ A = 320000 \times \left(\frac{19}{20}\right)^4 \\ A = 320000 \times \frac{130321}{160000} \\ A = 2 \times 130321 = 260642 \\ \text{Decrease} = 320000 - 260642 = 59358 $$

Exam Takeaway: Power 3 ya 4 aaye aur end values messy hon toh DS sabse pehla weapon hona chahiye.

questions.q: In a cricket series, Team A had a winning rate of $70\%$ after playing x matches. Then they lost 20 matches consecutively, and their winning rate fell to $50\%$. Find the total matches played by Team A before the losing streak?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM / Mixture Alligation Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab do alag alag chizon ka average/rate mix hokar ek naya overall rate bane, wahan hamesha Alligation lagta hai. Rate $70\%$ tha, haar me rate $0\%$ hai, aur mix hoke $50\%$ bana. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Alligation ratio nikal. Part 1: $70\%$, Part 2 (Losses): $0\%$. Overall: $50\%$. Cross subtract mar: $(50-0) : (70-50) = 50 : 20 = 5 : 2$. Yani (Initial Matches) : (Losing Streak Matches) ka ratio $5:2$ hona chahiye. Hame baad ke match pata hain = 20 (yani 2 unit = 20). Toh 5 unit = 50. Khel khatam! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic equation se jayega toh: $\frac{0.7x + 0}{x + 20} = 0.5$. Isko solve karega toh $0.7x = 0.5x + 10 \implies 0.2x = 10 \implies x = 50$. Time consuming hai par concept wahi hai. Exam Takeaway: Winning rate ya pass/fail average me jab constant naya judta hai toh Mixture concept hit kiya kar.
StateWin RateRatio
Initial$70\%$5 units (50 matches)
Losing Streak$0\%$2 units (20 matches)

questions.q: A spider climbed $62.5\%$ of the height of the pole in one hour and in the next hour it covered $12.5\%$ of the remaining height. If the pole's height is 192 m, then the distance climbed in the second hour is?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, fraction ka magic hai yahan. $62.5\%$ dekh ke dimaag me turant $\frac{5}{8}$ aur $12.5\%$ dekh ke $\frac{1}{8}$ flash hona chahiye. 'Remaining' likha hai matlab direct chain baneagi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Pehle ghante me makdi fraction cover kar chuki. Bachi kitni? Agle ghante me is bachi hui height ka multiplier laga. Kata-kuti me bhi time nahi lagta!

Mathematically :-
$$ H_1 = \\frac{5}{8} \\\\ H_{rem} = 1 - \\frac{5}{8} = \\frac{3}{8} \\\\ H_2 = \\frac{3}{8} \\times \\frac{1}{8} = \\frac{3}{64} \\\\ Distance = 192 \\times \\frac{3}{64} = 9 \\ m $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute values pe ja! Ye bhi chalega par fraction method se pen nahi chalana padta.

Mathematically :-
$$ D_1 = 192 \\times 0.625 = 120 \\ m \\\\ Rem = 192 - 120 = 72 \\ m \\\\ D_2 = 72 \\times 0.125 = 9 \\ m $$

Exam Takeaway: Successive percentage questions jisme 'remaining' likha ho, unhe hamesha fractional shifts banakar hi karna chahiye.

List I (Action Phase)List II (Fraction of Total)
A. Left after 1st Hour1. $\frac{3}{8}$
B. Climbed in 2nd Hour2. $\frac{3}{64}$
